sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04.10.2017 at about 7.30 p.m. while the petitioner was traveling on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50-Q-9750 met with an accident near Kote,
Thyarappa's Areca Garden, Nagenahalli Village with a tractor bearing registration No.KA-18-T-3760 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with respondent No.3 - Insurance Company.

Because of the accident, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Lacerated wound over scalp.

3. Fracture of scalp bone.

Because of the said injuries, the petitioner has lost his ability to smell, there was an air block in his brain which required a surgery to be cured and the treated Doctor has opined that petitioner is likely to get fits in future.
The petitioner also requires dental implants.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.4,00,871/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till depositing the amount (however, no interest is awarded on future medical expenses).
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
5. The petitioner has not let-in any evidence to prove his permanent physical disability before the Tribunal.

Hence, no compensation is awarded towards loss of future income and compensation is awarded only under the following heads:-
1. Pain & suffering Rs.50,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.2,30,871/-
3. Loss of future amenities and Rs.50,000/-
happiness 4. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
nourishment charges 5.

Future medical expenses Rs.50,000/-
TOTAL Rs.4,00,871/-
6.

In my opinion given the nature of injuries and the evidence let-in, the compensation awarded towards 'pain and suffering', 'medical expenses', 'attendant,
conveyance, NC: 2023:KHC:29385 food and nourishment charges' and 'future medical expenses' are appropriate.

As no evidence is let-in to prove the percentage of total body disability and how it affects his future earnings, no fault can be found with the order of the Tribunal in not awarding any compensation on the count of 'loss of future income'.
7.
However, it has been established that the petitioner has undergone surgery for removal of air block in the brain.

For that reason, he is entitled of some N Bhaskarachari vs L H Darshan on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178193436/

sentences.text: The accident is of the year 2017.
As per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Companies, the notional income is fixed at Rs.11,000/- per month.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to consider four months as the laid up period.
Thus, towards 'loss of income during laid up period', the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- (11,000x4).
The petitioner has suffered loss of smelling capability and he is required to undergo dental implants and he is having problem for chewing.
He has to live with the said deprivation for life.

Under the circumstance, towards 'loss of future amenities and happiness', I am of the opinion that it would be appropriate to enhance the compensation awarded under the head 'loss of future amenities and happiness' from Rs.50,000/- to Rs.1,25,000/-.

9. Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,19,871/- as against Rs.4,00,871/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,19,000/- (Rs.5,19,871 minus Rs.4,00,871/-).
10.
Given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.
